clue.text: Podgy man taking Latin on board at college

indicators.note: 'taking ... on board' means swallowing something up, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a man's name
L is the standard abbreviation for Latin
short for polytechnic, a kind of British college

explanation.surface: A plump man studies Latin while boarding at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship or a boarding school, but 'taking on board' means taking in. A poly was a polytechnic, a British higher-education college.
explanation.definitionFit: Roly-poly is an informal adjective for someone short, round and chubby, a close synonym.

clue.text: Sturdily built vehicle covered in rust?

indicators.note: something covered in another thing sits within it, wrapped on both sides

blocks.note: rust is a form of rot or decay
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A sturdy old vehicle is corroded all over with rust.
explanation.walkthrough: Rust is treated loosely as decay, which is the sense needed for the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust describes something strong and solidly constructed, a direct synonym of sturdily built.

clue.text: Bedding for animals born in a rubbish container

blocks.note: litter is straw or similar spread for animals to sleep on
b. is the abbreviation for born
taken as written

explanation.surface: Animal bedding ends up thrown away in a rubbish container.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter bin is a public receptacle for waste, so it is a container for rubbish.

clue.text: Wine - best round province sent over

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other
sending something over flips it, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: top means best
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: The finest wine from a region gets shipped abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is commonly called 'the Province' in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a grape variety and the wine made from it, such as Pinot Noir or Pinot Grigio.

clue.text: Tall striker?

blocks.note: surface reading: a lanky footballer or a tall boxer who hits hard
setter's reading: a tall timepiece in a wooden case that strikes the hours

explanation.walkthrough: A striker sounds like a footballer, but clocks strike too; the grandfather clock is the tall one.
explanation.definitionFit: A longcase clock, or grandfather clock, stands tall on the floor and chimes or strikes the hours.

clue.text: Church left with most of credit for football team

indicators.note: most of something means it is incomplete, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
L is the abbreviation for left
on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: A church abandons its credit arrangements to back a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: To buy on tick is British slang for buying on credit; TICK loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtic is a famous Glasgow football club, so it is an example of a football team.

clue.text: Holly, for example, is always common

blocks.note: ever means always
a common is a village green, public grassland

explanation.surface: Holly is a familiar plant you see everywhere at any time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' looks like an adjective but is the noun: a common is open public land, as is a village green.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly keeps its leaves through winter, making it an instance of a plant that never sheds foliage.

clue.text: Jewelled coronet, one worn by girl

indicators.note: something worn by a person is carried on them, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl wears a single jewelled coronet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a decorative jewelled headband worn by women, a kind of small crown.

clue.text: A number of men that can be put on board?

definitions.text: A number of men that can be put on board?

blocks.clueFragment: A number of men that can be put on board?
blocks.note: surface reading: a group of people allowed to embark on a ship

blocks.clueFragment: A number of men that can be put on board?
blocks.note: setter's reading: game pieces, called men, placed on a chequered playing surface

explanation.walkthrough: Pieces in board games are traditionally called men, and the board is the playing board, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of the playing pieces for the game of kings, queens and pawns, laid out on the board.

clue.text: Stick? No, sticker, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a tab is a small label stuck on

explanation.surface: Someone corrects themselves: not a stick but a sticker, now they think about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short rod, such as a relay runner's or conductor's stick.

clue.text: One dreamt about a famous cathedral

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone had a dream about a famous cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the great Gothic cathedral in Paris, so it is one particular famous cathedral.

clue.text: Fair play? That's the least one might hope for

definitions.text: Fair play? That's the least one might hope for

blocks.clueFragment: Fair play? That's the least one might hope for
blocks.note: surface reading: a sportsman asking only for just treatment

blocks.clueFragment: Fair play? That's the least one might hope for
blocks.note: setter's reading: someone reviewing stage drama who at minimum hopes the show is decent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair play' reads as sportsmanship, but here 'fair' means passable and 'play' is a stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer of stage productions goes to each performance hoping it will at least be passable.

clue.text: Picture show

blocks.note: first meaning: a striking sight or scene
second meaning: a lavish public display or performance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture show' looks like an old phrase for a cinema film; split it into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both an impressive visual scene and a grand public performance or display.

clue.text: Greek one on steamship providing cannabis

blocks.note: Gr. is the abbreviation for Greek
a means one
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A Greek sailor on a steamer supplies drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' simply means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is everyday slang for marijuana, the dried leaves of the hemp plant.

clue.text: Finish first, heaps better at running

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are on the move into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner is told to win, being far stronger at racing.
explanation.definitionFit: To breast the tape is to cross the finishing line in a race ahead of everyone, so to win.

clue.text: Expert peculiar to incomes?

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, so the letters are put into an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is there some specialist knowledge unique to earnings?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the expert is one who studies incomes, so the whole clue also points at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An economist is a specialist in money, production and trade, so a kind of expert.

clue.text: They provide ventilation for a starfish at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something supplies fresh air to a starfish living in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Air shafts are vertical passages that let fresh air into mines, buildings or ships.

clue.text: Spasmodic bird-watcher?

definitions.note: an adjective for a noun answer: read it as one who moves spasmodically

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who jerks or twitches
second meaning: an enthusiast who travels to spot rare birds

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a jumpy bird-watcher, but the two words point separately at one person who twitches and at a keen birder.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a twitcher is a dedicated birder chasing sightings of rare species; literally it is also one who twitches.

clue.text: The person to help improve one's outlook?

definitions.text: The person to help improve one's outlook?

blocks.clueFragment: The person to help improve one's outlook?
blocks.note: surface reading: a counsellor who makes someone more optimistic

blocks.clueFragment: The person to help improve one's outlook?
blocks.note: setter's reading: someone who makes the view through the panes clearer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlook' means attitude on the surface, but literally it is the view from a house.
explanation.definitionFit: This tradesperson washes glass panes on buildings, literally giving a clearer view out.

clue.text: Mate has half a day to finish

indicators.note: half of a word means only its first three of six letters are kept

blocks.note: Friday is a day of six letters
end means finish

explanation.surface: A pal has a short working day before knocking off.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is informal British for a companion or pal, a close synonym.

clue.text: Work carried out after retirement needs time

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so after that the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
to meet an obligation is to carry it out

explanation.surface: Taking a job after retirement requires spare time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests temping in retirement; instead the whole of 'Work carried out' is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo in music is the speed of the beat, also simply called the time.

clue.text: Male behind promoted copper?

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoting something moves it upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
late means behind time

explanation.surface: A man who was a lagging police constable has been promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but the question mark warns it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a chemical element of the kind that conducts electricity and is malleable, an example.

clue.text: God to a Führer is ridiculous

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the umlaut ignored

explanation.surface: Treating a dictator as a deity is absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Father is a way of addressing the Lord, from the opening words of the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: Quarrel with a grocer, initially in French street

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
in places one piece inside the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
rue is French for street
the opening letter of grocer

explanation.surface: Someone rows with a shopkeeper on a street in France.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes inside RUE after the R, and A goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to dispute angrily, so it works as a verb meaning quarrel.

clue.text: One way of getting out on appeal?

definitions.text: One way of getting out on appeal?

blocks.clueFragment: One way of getting out on appeal?
blocks.note: surface reading: a prisoner being released after a court appeal

blocks.clueFragment: One way of getting out on appeal?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a mode of dismissal in cricket, given when fielders appeal to the umpire

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is out only when fielders appeal ('Howzat?'); a batsman who knocks over their own stumps is dismissed this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit wicket is one of the recognised modes of dismissal in cricket, when batters strike their own stumps.

clue.text: Tactless remark made by senior electrician, cut short

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its tail, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the gaffer is the chief electrician on a film set

explanation.surface: A senior electrician makes a clumsy remark and is interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaffer is also British slang for a boss, which helps.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder, especially an indiscreet or embarrassing comment.

clue.text: Pawn must escape from bishop to make one tell

indicators.note: escaping from something means leaving it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn
a prelate is a senior churchman such as a bishop

explanation.surface: A chess pawn must flee a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Pawn and bishop suggest chess, but the bishop is a churchman here.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate or recount it, so relate means tell.

clue.text: Retrieved data from battered cases, including chapter by editor

indicators.note: something battered is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
including means taking something in among the others

blocks.note: taken as written
c. is the abbreviation for chapter
ed. is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor recovers information from damaged files that hold a chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Accessed is the computing verb for opening or retrieving stored information from a file or system.
